newsitem.title: CHINA: New China copper plant '97 output seen at 70,000 T.
newsitem.headline: New China copper plant '97 output seen at 70,000 T.

text.p: The Jinlong smelter being built in China's central Anhui province is expected to produce 70,000 tonnes of copper in 1997, top company officials said on Monday.

The project, in which Japan's Sumitomo Metal Mining Co has a 20 percent stake, would be completed by the end of 1996 and was to begin full operation by mid-February, said Kotaro Tomino, the smelter's assistant general manager.
The smelter would achieve its full capacity of 100,000 tonnes of refined copper in 1998, Tomino said.
Sumitomo Corp and Itochu Corp also have stakes in the project, Tomino said.
The smelter would buy copper concentrate mainly from abroad, but would not buy copper concentrate with high levels of precious metals such as gold and silver, he said.
If the smelter extracted gold and silver from the copper it would be forced to sell it to China's central bank at a 10 percent discount, he said.
"The regulations on precious metals, such as gold and silver, are very severe," he said.
The Jinlong plant would have an annual capacity of 260,000 tonnes of sulphuric acid, he said, adding that sulphuric acid production in 1997 would be around 70 percent of final capacity.
